title: Influence of the cutting balloon and drug-coated balloon angioplasty on the acute and long-term outcome of endovascular shunt interventions
summary:
Frequent complications after shunt installation for dialysis include stenosis, dilatation or infection.
Stenosis of the shunt can occur at various points in the shunt and can be treated by intervention.
However, recurrent interventions are often necessary to maintain shunt function.
The patency rates after conventional balloon angioplasty are low.
With the so-called Cutting Balloon, another balloon system is available for the treatment of stenoses.
The Cutting Balloon is an unyielding balloon on whose surface longitudinally arranged microsurgical blades are applied. This causes an incision in the vessel wall during dilatation and thus even hard stenoses can be dilated with low balloon pressures. An important development in endovascular therapy was the combination of balloon dilatation and local administration of an antiproliferative drug in the form of drug coated balloons.
In recent years,  drug coated balloons has shown impressive results after femoropopliteal interventions.
This also offers the potential to improve patency rates after shunt interventions.
On the other hand, a recently published study led to uncertainties. It showed an increased risk of mortality within 5 years after application of paclitaxel-coated balloons/stent in femoropopliteal lesions in patients with normal or slightly impaired renal function. 
The aim of the present retrospective, monocentric study is to evaluate the acute and long-term results of treatment of shunt stenosis and occlusion using cutting balloon and paclitaxel-coated balloon angioplasty compared to treatment using conventional uncoated balloon angioplasty.
conditions: Mechanical complication of vascular dialysis catheter
